title: Compute crystal binding energy per atom
action: Perform first-principles DFT calculations using the GGA-PW91 exchange-correlation functional to optimize the unit cells of cumulene and polyyne, and obtain the total energy of an isolated carbon atom in a large periodic box. From the converged total energies, derive the crystal binding energy per atom: W = (2*E_atom - E_cell)/2, and compute the binding energy difference (polyyne minus cumulene) in meV/atom. Additionally, compute the fundamental (direct) band gaps for cumulene and polyyne, the zero-frequency real part of the dielectric constant (static ε₁) for both phases, and determine the most stable polyyne supercell size by computing total energies for N=2 through N=9 and identifying the global minimum. Write all results to total_energies.json.
description: Crystal binding energies per atom for cumulene and polyyne, binding-energy difference, band gaps, static dielectric constants, and supercell stability analysis.
output_schema: {"cumulene": {"total_energy_cell": float (eV), "binding_energy_per_atom": float (eV/atom)}, "polyyne": {"total_energy_cell": float (eV), "binding_energy_per_atom": float (eV/atom)}, "binding_energy_difference_polyyne_minus_cumulene": float (meV/atom), "cumulene_band_gap_eV": float, "polyyne_band_gap_eV": float, "cumulene_static_epsilon_real": float, "polyyne_static_epsilon_real": float, "supercell_optimal_N": int, "supercell_energy_at_optimal_N_eV": float, "supercell_energy_at_N4_eV": float}

title: Compute tensile stiffness of cumulene and polyyne
action: Using the equilibrium structures of cumulene and polyyne, perform DFT total energy calculations for a series of uniaxial strains along the chain direction. Fit the energy vs strain curve to a second-order polynomial and extract the tensile stiffness C = (1/a) d²E/dε², where a is the equilibrium cell length. Write the stiffness values to tensile_stiffness.json.
description: Tensile stiffness (second derivative of energy with respect to strain) for cumulene and polyyne in eV/Å.

title: Compute phonon dispersion of cumulene and assess dynamical stability
action: Using the optimized cumulene unit cell, compute the phonon dispersion along the high-symmetry path G–Q–Z (as denoted in the paper). Identify the lowest phonon frequency and determine whether any imaginary (negative) frequencies exist. Output the minimum frequency, a boolean flag, and the list of frequencies at high-symmetry points in THz to phonon_frequencies.json.
description: Minimum phonon frequency in THz, a flag indicating the presence of imaginary modes, and the frequencies at high-symmetry points for cumulene.
